topic: Part 4 §4.2.4 E-PRED-C paragraph rebuild (EXP-603 P5): Van Camp→Mansinha citation repair in “What the published record actually shows”
our_argument_summary: The rebuilt §4.2.4 paragraph asserts: the dome cites “Van Camp 1999. 0.0 μGal. Confirms electromagnetic, not gravitational.”; no Van Camp-authored eclipse-gravimetry paper exists under that citation; the peer-reviewed record of the Membach null is Mansinha, Ducarme, Hinderer, Meurers & van Ruymbeke (2001), J. Geod. Soc. Japan 47(1), 387–391, DOI 10.11366/sokuchi1954.47.387; Michel Van Camp operates the Membach SG for the Royal Observatory of Belgium but is not an author; the paper found no identifiable eclipse-related change above ambient noise, setting γ < 10^-16 m²/kg; the “electromagnetic, not gravitational” conclusion is the dome's addition; the null confirms Newton, not the dome.

holes_found.description: Inoculation gap on the negative existence claim. A dome defender's most natural comeback to “No Van Camp-authored eclipse-gravimetry paper exists under that citation” is: “Van Camp (1999) DOES exist — ‘Measuring seismic normal modes with the GWR C021 superconducting gravimeter’, Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. (DOI 10.1016/s0031-9201(99)00120-x) — a 1999 Van Camp paper about the very Membach instrument.” Our claim survives because that paper contains no eclipse analysis and no 0.0 µGal result (verified via Crossref this run), but the paragraph never names it, so a reader who finds it may think we missed it. Bonus: that PEPI paper is almost certainly the second half of the chimera — it explains both the dome's “Van Camp 1999” shorthand AND where our own withdrawn “Phys. Earth Planet. Inter.” journal attribution came from. Naming it converts a potential gotcha into a stronger argument.
holes_found.recommendation: Add ~1 sentence to the parenthetical, e.g.: “(Van Camp's real 1999 paper — ‘Measuring seismic normal modes with the GWR C021 superconducting gravimeter’, Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. — describes the Membach instrument but contains no eclipse analysis; the dome's shorthand most plausibly fuses that instrument paper with Mansinha et al.'s eclipse result.)”

holes_found.description: Quotation normalization: the paragraph quotes the dome as “Van Camp 1999. 0.0 μGal. Confirms electromagnetic, not gravitational.” inside quotation marks, but the dome's actual printed text (raw-text/02-wins.txt:90) uses ASCII “uGal”, not “μGal”. In a paragraph whose whole point is faithful-quotation discipline (we just corrected ourselves for putting words in the dome's mouth), even glyph normalization inside quote marks is worth avoiding.
holes_found.recommendation: Either render the quote byte-faithful (“0.0 uGal”) or move the µ-normalization outside the quotation.

holes_found.description: The appositive “consistent with standard physics predictions” is attached to the γ < 10^-16 bound sentence, but the abstract's own framing is “consistent with the majority of recent estimates of γ from eclipse observations with spring gravimeters, but substantially higher than the γ<10^-22 … from lunar laser ranging.” The null being the standard-physics prediction is true (and stated separately later); attaching the consistency clause to the bound invites a pedant to say the paper frames the bound against other γ estimates, not against ‘standard physics predictions’.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional half-sentence tweak: attach “consistent with standard physics” to the null result rather than the γ bound, or cite the abstract's own comparison.

stronger_arguments.description: Name Van Camp's real 1999 PEPI instrument paper as the likely chimera source (see moderate hole). It simultaneously (a) pre-empts the defender gotcha, (b) explains the dome's shorthand charitably and precisely, and (c) accounts for the journal name in our own withdrawn fabricated citation — closing the loop on the EXP-603 correction narrative.
sources: 10.1016/s0031-9201(99)00120-x (Van Camp 1999, PEPI — GWR C021 Membach instrument paper, no eclipse content; Crossref-verified this run)

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome's “Van Camp 1999” shorthand is closer to a real citation than our rebuilt paragraph lets on: Van Camp (1999), PEPI — ‘Measuring seismic normal modes with the GWR C021 superconducting gravimeter’ (10.1016/s0031-9201(99)00120-x) — is a genuine 1999 paper about the exact Membach instrument that recorded the eclipse null (Crossref query, this review run). And the underlying empirical claim is right: the Membach SG recorded no eclipse-related gravity change in August 1999, exactly as Mansinha et al. 2001 report (J-STAGE abstract, this run: ‘no identifiable eclipse related change above the ambient noise’).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A correct null with a garbled attribution still refutes the dome: under the dome's own κ = 1.677 nT/µGal coupling (part4.html §4.2.4, E-PRED-C discussion), the eclipse should have produced a measurable gravity signature, so the verified 0.0 µGal null (10.11366/sokuchi1954.47.387) is evidence against the model, and the ‘Confirms electromagnetic, not gravitational’ gloss remains the dome's own addition — no such conclusion appears in the Mansinha abstract fetched this run.

text_fingerprint.paragraph_anchor: What the published record actually shows

deeper_analysis: EXP-603 P5 is a clean, verified repair and materially strengthens §4.2.4: every load-bearing element of the rebuilt paragraph (DOI resolution, exact author list, journal/volume/pages, four-station count, verbatim noise quote, γ bound, dome's actual printed text, Van Camp-as-operator-not-author) was independently reproduced this run from primary sources rather than trusted from the EXP. The one structural weakness is asymmetric inoculation: the paragraph proves the cited paper does not exist but does not tell the reader what DOES exist under ‘Van Camp 1999’, leaving the strongest defender comeback unaddressed in text. This is a strengthening opportunity, not an error — the existence claim is correctly scoped (‘eclipse-gravimetry paper… under that citation’) and survives the gotcha. The inline-correction strategy (owning our prior fabricated-attribution error loudly) is the right call given our Part 1.4 attacks on the dome's silent edits; the correction in WIN-013 (P2) and the withdrawal in part6 (P6, queue 504) are cross-consistent with this paragraph. No verdict implications: §4.2.4's E-PRED-C conclusion (null favors standard model) is unchanged and now rests on a resolvable source.
